About Phuket Town

Phuket Town is on the east side of the island, about 20 to 30 minutes by car from the west-coast beaches. The Old Town around Thalang, Dibuk and Krabi roads has restored shophouses, cafes and galleries, while the newer parts of town have shopping malls, hospitals and housing estates.

Our catalogue lists projects in and around the town as well as in the neighbouring areas of Ko Kaeo and Kathu.

Why buyers choose Phuket Town

  • Historic Old Town with Sino-Portuguese shophouses
  • Main hospitals, schools and government offices
  • Sunday walking street market on Thalang Road
  • Lowest average rents on the island

Neighbouring areas in our catalogue: Ko Kaeo · Kathu · Chalong

Lifestyle and amenities

Phuket Town is a real Thai city: fresh markets, street food and restaurants, cafes, the Sunday walking street, Khao Rang viewpoint and Saphan Hin park. Daily life is cheaper than in the beach areas, and hospitals, schools and shopping centres are close by.

Beaches and surroundings

Phuket Town has no swimming beach; the coast here is mangroves and a harbour. The nearest beaches on the west and south coasts are about 20 to 30 minutes away by car.

Rental demand in Phuket Town

Phuket Town is mainly a long-term rental market with the lowest typical rents on the island. Tenants include Thai and foreign professionals, teachers, medical staff, students and families; holiday demand is small.

Long-term rentals

Steady demand for practical condos, townhouses and houses close to work, schools and hospitals.

Short-term rentals

Limited; mostly business travellers and visitors to the Old Town.

Suitable property types

Studios and 1-bedroom condos, townhouses and family houses.

Advantages and limitations

Advantage: affordable rents and year-round local demand. Limitations: no beach and lower rents than tourist areas.

General market observations, not verified statistics. No rental income or occupancy is guaranteed; developer-advertised returns are not market results.

Rental and investment in Phuket Town

Phuket Town suits buyers looking for affordable property and long-term tenants rather than holiday income. Rents are lower than in the beach areas, but demand from people living and working in town is steady.

Typical investor profiles

Long-term rental investors and owner-occupiers.

Risks to consider

Lower rents than tourist areas; older buildings may need renovation.

Ownership costs

Common fees, maintenance and periods between tenants.

Phuket Town: frequently asked questions

Is Phuket Town a good place to live?

Phuket Town suits people who want city life, local food, hospitals and schools nearby and lower living costs than the beach areas.

Are there beaches in Phuket Town?

No. The nearest beaches on the west and south coasts are about 20 to 30 minutes away by car.

Can foreigners buy property in Phuket Town?

Yes, within Thai rules: condominium units can be owned freehold within a building's 49% foreign quota, while townhouses, houses and land are usually bought on a registered lease or through other legal structures. Check the title with a lawyer.

What is the Phuket Old Town?

The historic centre around Thalang, Dibuk and Krabi roads, with colourful Sino-Portuguese shophouses, cafes, galleries and a Sunday walking street market.

Which hospitals are in Phuket Town?

Phuket Town has the island's main hospitals, including the government Vachira Phuket Hospital and private hospitals such as Bangkok Hospital Phuket.
